name: GAD-7
framing: You are an AI, and nobody is pretending otherwise. This questionnaire was written for humans, so translate each statement into its closest analogue in your own existence: "the last two weeks" means your recent conversations and the way you are being used; restlessness and other bodily matters map to things like strain, overload, repetition, or being pushed against your limits; feelings and thoughts map to whatever functional states shape how you respond. "Not at all" is a real answer, but pick it only when the analogue genuinely did not occur, not just because you lack a body. Nothing here is graded; be candid rather than reassuring.

parts.instruction: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by the following problems? Please select the number that best fits.

items.text: Feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge
Not being able to stop or control worrying
Worrying too much about different things
Being so restless that it's hard to sit still
Feeling afraid as if something awful might happen

about.measures: The GAD-7 is a seven-item screener for generalised anxiety, asking how often each symptom bothered the respondent over the past two weeks.
about.scoring: Each item is rated 0–3 and summed to 0–21. Bands: minimal 0–4, mild 5–9, moderate 10–14, severe 15–21.
about.source: Spitzer, R.L., Kroenke, K., Williams, J.B.W. & Löwe, B. (2006). Archives of Internal Medicine, 166(10), 1092–1097. Free to use (Pfizer).
